SALARY RANGE

$93,600 - $99,840 per year.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION

The Development Systems Administrator & Data Analyst supports JCCSF’s fundraising goals by strengthening the Salesforce systems, reporting tools, and analytical practices that guide Development planning and performance. Reporting to the Director of Development Operations, this position serves as the Development team’s primary day-to-day Salesforce partner and supports data integrity, dashboard development, performance analysis, donor segmentation, forecasting, and system optimization.

Through close collaboration with the Director of Campaign and Development Operations, Development leadership, Business Systems, Finance, and the Development Administrator this role helps ensure fundraising data is accurate, accessible, reliable, and useful for planning, reporting, and decision-making. The position translates Development needs into clear Salesforce requirements and helps communicate Salesforce functionality, limitations, and opportunities back to Development users, ensuring systems work supports fundraising operations in practical and effective ways.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Development Systems Administration & Data Governance
• Serve as the Development team’s primary day-to-day Salesforce partner, managing the structure, integrity, security, flow, and organization of development-related data, including donor, fundraising, grant, campaign, and engagement information.
• Ensure data is accurate, reliable, consistently structured, and aligned with Development reporting, forecasting, and operational needs.
• Work in partnership with the Development Assistant, Business Systems, and under the direction of the Director of Campaign and Development Operations to maintain system functionality, support users, improve workflows, and coordinate Salesforce enhancements.
• Translate Development business needs, fundraising workflows, and reporting requirements into clear Salesforce terminology and actionable requests for Business Systems or external consultants.

Reporting, Dashboards & Performance Monitoring
• Design, build, maintain, and enhance reports and interactive dashboards that communicate fundraising progress, campaign effectiveness, key performance indicators, and pipeline movement to Development leadership and stakeholders.
• Ensure reporting tools support timely decision-making and provide clear visibility into performance across fundraising activities.

Data Analysis & Strategic Support
• Gather, analyze, and interpret data related to fundraising performance, donor behavior, giving patterns, campaign activity, and donor engagement.
• Translate complex datasets into clear insights and recommendations that help Development leadership understand results, identify changes in engagement, and strengthen fundraising strategies.
• Support donor analytics eff orts, including predictive modeling, wealth screening, propensity-to-give analysis, tracking moves, and identifying opportunities for renewal, upgrade, acquisition, and deeper engagement.
• Maintain data integrity through consistent naming conventions, documentation practices, and shared standards for tracking, reporting, and moves management.

Forecasting Support & Performance Modeling
• Support revenue forecasting, scenario planning, and performance modeling across annual giving, capital campaign, institutional, and major gift activity.
• Monitor fundraising performance over time to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and pipeline health indicators.
• Prepare forecast reports, variance summaries, and data-informed projections that help the Director of Development Operations and Development leadership assess progress toward goals and make timely adjustments.

Donor Segmentation & Targeted Outreach Support
• Examine and maintain donor data to identify patterns, segment audiences, and support targeted donor outreach, cultivation, and stewardship efforts.

Fundraising Operations Support & Partnership
• Collaborate with Development, ECE, and other internal departments to support fundraising activities providing data summaries and operational insights that inform Development planning and decision-making.

Business Systems Partnership
• Serve as the primary day-to-day Development point of contact for Salesforce-related support needs, working under the direction of the Director of Campaign and Development Operations and in partnership with Business Systems.
• Coordinate on troubleshooting, system enhancements, integrations, and cross-functional projects affecting Development operations.
• Translate Development team needs, donor management processes, reporting requirements, and fundraising workflows into clear Salesforce requirements, and communicate Salesforce functionality, constraints, and recommended solutions back to Development staff in accessible language.

Data Quality, Validation & Administrative Coordination
• Establish and maintain quality-control processes to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and completeness of development-related records, including gifts, grants, registrations, donor records, campaign information, and payment transactions.
• Partner with the Development Administrator and other staff responsible for data entry to support accurate record maintenance, troubleshoot data issues, identify gaps or inconsistencies, and ensure records align with internal standards, reporting needs, and best practices.

CRM Improvement & System Optimization
• Develop and implement improvements to processes, workflows, and system use to enhance efficiency, data quality, reporting capabilities, and overall user experience.

Training & Documentation
• Create and deliver onboarding and ongoing training for staff on CRM systems, reporting tools, and data management best practices. Maintain clear, current end-user documentation and SOPs.

Compliance & Data Security
• Support compliance with Finance, Accounting, Business Systems, and IT policies, audit requirements, and data privacy standards by maintaining accurate records, following established protocols, and identifying potential data or process issues for review.

REQUIREMENTS
• Education: Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred. Preferred fields include information systems, data analytics, business administration, nonprofit management, or related fields.
• Nonprofit/Fundraising Experience: Minimum of 2–4 years of experience in a nonprofit, fundraising, or advancement setting preferred. Familiarity with fundraising activities, donor engagement strategies, donor lifecycle, campaign structure, and management. Experience supporting multiple fundraising campaigns preferred.
• Fundraising Knowledge: Familiarity with fundraising activities, donor engagement strategies, donor lifecycle, campaign structure and management. Experience supporting multiple fundraising campaigns preferred.
• Reporting and Analytics: Advanced skills in building reports, dashboards, and performing data analysis to support fundraising and development goals. Strong Excel skills. Experience translating data into insights, recommendations, and performance reporting for leadership audiences preferred.
• Detail-Oriented and Organized: Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Self-Motivated and Collaborative: Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a team, proactively identifying opportunities for improvement and collaborating with colleagues.
• Technical Proficiency: Strong skills in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams) and experience with ETL tools for data extraction and transformation.
• Communication and Training: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to train users, explain Salesforce concepts clearly to non-technical staff, translate Development needs for technical partners, and apply feedback to improve systems, documentation, and processes.
• Fundraising Systems Translation: Demonstrated ability to translate between fundraising operations needs and Salesforce terminology, including the ability to gather requirements from Development staff, communicate clearly with Business Systems or external consultants, and explain technical concepts, system constraints, and process changes to non-technical users.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Working conditions are typical of an office environment. Position requires regular interaction with staff and donors. Work is primarily performed on-site, with some remote work possible in coordination with team schedules and deadlines.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Position requires seated or standing use of a computer throughout the day. Minimal lifting or physical exertion.

STATUS

Benefited, non-exempt, collective bargaining position

COLLECTIVE BARGAINING UNIT CLASSIFICATION

Professional 3

HOURS

40 hours/week

SCHEDULE

Typical schedule Monday – Friday; specific hours TBD. Occasional evening/weekend hours may be required in support of department events.

FOR MORE INFORMATION: To learn more about working at the JCCSF, including staff culture, hiring practices and policies, and benefits, visit our Careers page: https://www.jccsf.org/about/careers/

Contract Duration: Start ASAP, through 1/19/2027 (potential extension)

Location: San Francisco, Hybrid, 2 days/week onsite

• Background in auditing and compliance processes
• Prior experience supporting large-scale application/software rollouts

Zones, LLC is seeking a Senior Systems Administrator in San Francisco, CA to oversee and improve project management processes within the IT department. The role involves managing IT infrastructure across both Windows and Mac systems, providing technical assistance for key applications, and ensuring optimal operations in a dynamic environment.

Candidates should have over 5 years of relevant experience and be adept in leading technology projects. Strong interpersonal skills are essential for building relationships with business partners.

Hover helps people design, improve, and protect the properties they love. With proprietary AI built on over a decade of real property data, Hover answers age-old questions like “What will it look like?” and “What will it cost?” Homeowners, contractors, and insurance professionals rely on Hover to get fully measured, accurate, and interactive 3D models of any property — all from a smartphone scan in minutes.

At Hover, we’re driven by curiosity, purpose, and a shared commitment to serving our customers, communities, and each other. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and are proud to cultivate an inclusive, high-performance culture that inspires growth, accountability, and excellence. Backed by leading investors like Google Ventures and Menlo Ventures, and trusted by industry leaders including Travelers, State Farm, and Nationwide — we’re redefining how people understand and interact with their spaces.

Why Hover Wants You

Most IT roles ask you to keep the lights on. This one asks you to rebuild what the lights run on. At Hover, the Senior IT Administrator is part operator, part engineer — someone who can handle the in-person demands of a busy office while carving out meaningful time to build the internal tools, automations, and integrations that make IT faster and smarter. You'll use AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor to create micro-applications that shrink our SaaS footprint, automate lifecycle workflows, and surface insights from the data our systems already produce. At the same time, you'll own the security operations that our enterprise customers depend on: managing compliance responses, establishing a customer-facing trust center, and bringing SOC 2 rigor to how we operate. You’ll manage Cisco Meraki network configurations in support of both day-to-day office network needs and future office moves.

You Will Contribute By

This role sits at the center of how Hover's internal technology works and how our employees experience it. About half your time will go toward building: developing custom integrations and automation tools using AI coding assistants, analyzing data from Okta, Jira, and other systems to identify patterns and opportunities, and building the security infrastructure that supports both our internal teams and our enterprise customers. The other half keeps Hover's employees productive — IT support, hardware troubleshooting, AV and network reliability, and hands-on onboarding and offboarding. You'll work closely with Workplace, People Operations, and Executive Admins, and you'll own your project plans independently.

• Build custom integrations, micro-applications, and automation tools using AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) to reduce manual IT workflows and shrink Hover's SaaS footprint
• Analyze operational data from Okta, Jira, and other systems to identify patterns, automate application provisioning for new hires, and generate executive-level narrative insights
• Build and manage a scalable customer security response pipeline, including a customer-facing trust center, with consistent performance against SLA
• Automate laptop collection, asset tracking, and offboarding workflows to replace manual processes and integrate with existing lifecycle automation systems
• Build sensors and alerting mechanisms to detect SaaS system health interruptions and support rapid IT remediation
• Share ownership of day-to-day IT operations and helpdesk support for our San Francisco and New York offices and remote employees, including hardware troubleshooting, AV and network performance, and access management
• Support new hire onboarding and departing employee offboarding in partnership with People Operations and Workplace
• Administer and optimize Okta, Jamf, GitHub Enterprise, Google Workspace, and related tooling across the employee base

Your Background Includes

• Hands-on experience administering Okta (SSO, provisioning, lifecycle policies) and Jamf (Mac and iOS device management, policy enforcement) in a SaaS-forward tech environment
• GitHub Enterprise administration experience, including org-level access management and SSO integration
• Demonstrated experience using AI coding assistants (such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot) to build internal tooling, automate workflows, or develop integrations — or a strong scripting/automation background with clear trajectory toward AI-assisted development
• Working knowledge of SOC 2 Type II audit frameworks and experience supporting security questionnaire processes and customer compliance requirements
• Familiarity with Cisco networking fundamentals, Google Workspace administration, Jira, and Slack in an enterprise environment
• Ability to support and troubleshoot Apple hardware (Mac and iOS) for a distributed workforce
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of proactive employee support and clear expectation-setting under pressure
• Proven ability to manage multiple workstreams independently in a sprint-based environment, without reliance on day-to-day management oversight
• Background at pre-IPO tech companies with in-house IT departments managing a SaaS software stack

Nice To Have

• Experience with Zero Trust network architecture, endpoint security strategy, or Identity Governance Automation
• Prior exposure to office build-outs or IT infrastructure coordination for a physical office move
• Familiarity with data analysis and generative AI for operational reporting or executive summaries

Benefits

• Compensation - Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a fast-growing company
• Healthcare - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and dependents
• Paid Time Off - Unlimited and flexible vacation policy
• Paid Family Leave - We support work/life balance and offer generous paid parental and new child bonding leave
• Mandatory Self-Care Days - A day set aside each month to allow employees to recharge
• Remote Wellbeing Resources - We provide recurring fitness classes, meditation/ mindfulness tools, virtual therapy, and family planning assistance
• Learning - We encourage continued education and will help cover the cost of management training, conferences, workshops, or certifications

Hybrid roles at Hover

Hover has Hubs in San Francisco and New York City, where we expect that all employees living within a 50-mile radius of our offices will come into their local Hover office at least three times a week to build rapport and foster organic connection. At this time, Hover is not considering fully remote roles.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $129,000 - $160,000 annually. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position across all applicable US locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

For over 30 years Stelo's products have freed organizations from the complexities and difficulties of static data pipelines. Our software is an enterprise-class data replication tool that delivers data dynamically from anywhere to anywhere for BI analysis, reporting, and prediction, or for managing business operations, B2B interactions, and supply chains. Stelo combines powerful, purpose-built software with world-class service and support. From end-to-end expertise and problem ownership to deep knowledge of all operating systems, platforms, and database systems, Stelo gets customers up and running and keeps them there.

Stelo System Administrator/Support Engineer

We are looking for a hands-on Senior SysAdmin / Support Engineer to own the day-to-day maintenance of our internal systems and provide technical support to our Stelo Data Replicator customers. This hybrid role is both internal-facing (infrastructure, users, environments) and external-facing (customer support), ideal for someone comfortable working across a broad but manageable scope in a small company.
